articles.title: President Donald Trump’s childhood home sells for $2 million
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Donald Trump's childhood home has sold for nearly $2 million after a renovation transformed the New York City residence from a mold-ridden cat den to a modern abode.

articles.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says AI industry needs to give safety measures time to catch up
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — The CEO of Anthropic said Saturday the artificial-intelligence industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without it, Dario Amodei warned AI could be capable within six to 12 months of leading a swarm that could take over the entire internet, among other risks.

articles.title: ‘Elderly man’ rescued from midtown Toronto fire
articles.summary: Toronto police say an “elderly man” was rescued from a fire in midtown on Saturday morning. Emergency crews were called to the Davisville neighbourhood, near Millwood Road and Forman Avenue just before 10 a.m. Police say several homes were evacuated for safety. No injuries were immediately reported. Roads in the area were closed while crews […]

articles.title: Former car insurance broker is charged with defrauding the public
articles.summary: A man who is accused of selling dozens of fraudulent car insurance policies in the Greater Toronto Area has been charged. According to Peel Regional Police, 25-year-old Muhammad Raahim of Mississauga knowingly provided victims with “falsified proof of insurance documents.” “To date, police have identified 15 incidents connected to the scheme, with reported victim losses […]

articles.title: Man accused of making antisemitic social media posts is charged with 3 hate crimes
articles.summary: A man from Stoney Creek is facing several hate crime charges following an investigation into what police describe as “hate-related content” posted online. The Hamilton Police Hate Crime Unit says it launched an investigation after receiving a report about “concerning content” posted to an account on the social media platform X in July 2025. Police […]

articles.title: Two uniforms, one deadly morning: A Mississauga firefighter and former soldier reflects on 9/11
articles.summary: Twenty-five years after the terror attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, Shawn Matheson recalls viewing them through two different lenses: as a firefighter in Mississauga, Ont., and as a Canadian reservist. The tragedy would take him to funerals at Ground Zero, foreshadow the war in Afghanistan and reveal the lasting emotional cost borne by soldiers and first responders alike.

articles.title: Reliance on visual inspections may have played role in GO train derailment at Union Station: report
articles.summary: A new report has found an overreliance on visual inspections of the train tracks may have contributed to the derailment of a GO Transit train at Toronto's Union Station that disrupted commuter travel for days earlier this year.

articles.title: Stellantis signs MOU with Canadian armoured vehicle maker on potential sale of Brampton, Ont., plant
articles.summary: Automaker Stellantis says it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel on a potential sale of its idled Brampton, Ont., assembly plant.

articles.title: 'Destruction is not necessary': Gardeners fight city plan to relocate 30-year-old community plot
articles.summary: A 30-year-old community garden in downtown Toronto will soon have to pull up its stakes and move, as the city prepares to transform a piece of land into an eight-storey supportive housing project.

articles.title: Streaming fatigue? Inside the new Criterion retail store in Toronto
articles.summary: A massive selection of DVD, Blu-ray, and 4K physical movies lining every wall has opened in Toronto, curated by Criterion Collection, a film company based in New York. CBC’s Mercedes Gaztambide takes you inside its first retail store in the city.

articles.title: Brad Bradford says he will put a Toronto police outpost in Union Station if he’s elected mayor
articles.summary: Brad Bradford has promised a Toronto police outpost at Union Station as part of his mayoral campaign platform.
